---
title: "No bed level in the net file; the bed level goes in as samples"
---

`write_ugrid` writes the 2D mesh without `Mesh2d_node_z` and `Mesh2d_face_z`. The bed
level is given to D-Flow FM as samples (`x y z` per cell centre) in the field file,
not as a value per cell or node in the net file.

Up to 0.1.1 both variables were written with -999 for every node and face, as the
D-HYDRO mesh generator export does. That caused two problems, found on 2026-11-12 with
D-HYDRO Suite 2026.02:

- **hydrolib.** `mesh2d_from_netcdf` reads the -999 arrays into the network. A clip with
  MeshKernel (`mesh2d_clip`) removes nodes but leaves `mesh2d_node_z` at its old length,
  and saving the model (`dimr.save`) fails with a shape mismatch.
- **D-HYDRO GUI.** The GUI rebuilds the 2D cells from nodes and edges and also closes
  small gaps, so it can have more cells than the file. A bed level per cell
  (`mesh2d_face_z`) then no longer fits and the import fails ("number of values is not
  equal to multiple of all argument values"). On the Geul model (277,206 cells) MeshKernel
  also built one extra cell on reading, in another order.

## Considered Options

- **Keep the -999 variables (the export structure).** Rejected for the two problems above.
- **Write the bed level per cell (`mesh2d_face_z`) from a raster.** Rejected: D-Flow FM
  and DIMR use it, but the GUI rejects it once it rebuilds the cells.
- **Write the cells as MeshKernel rebuilds them, so the GUI agrees.** Rejected: that
  adds cells on gaps that the model build removes on purpose, and it ties the file to
  one MeshKernel version.

## Consequences

- The net file has the structure of the D-HYDRO export minus the two bed level
  variables; the structure test compares with the old writer's file on that basis.
- The documentation (Use the mesh in D-HYDRO) gives the bed level as `bodem_2d.xyz`
  with two `[Initial] bedlevel` blocks at the top of the field file, `bedLevType = 1`.
  Tested on the Geul model: D-Flow FM gives every cell exactly the sampled level, and
  the model loads in the GUI.
- `read_ugrid` still reads files that have the variables; it ignores them.
- A net file without bed level and without samples runs with `BedLevUni` everywhere,
  without a warning.
